source: Screenwriting form reference — scene shapes and the coverage each one implies
_note: Each entry is a dramatic structure and the shot grammar it asks for, written as an original worked example. No copyrighted screenplay text is reproduced; where a technique is associated with a filmmaker it is named as attribution.

entries.name: Cold Open
entries.summary: Start inside the event. Establish nothing; explain later or never.
entries.detail:
INT. STAIRWELL — NIGHT

A woman takes the stairs two at a time. She is not running from anything we can see.

She stops. Listens.

Below her, three floors down, a door closes.

She keeps climbing.

— The rule: no establishing shot, no name, no context. The audience's first job is to work out what is happening, and that work is what buys their attention. Coverage starts tight and only widens once the question has been planted.

prompt: open on action already in progress, no establishing wide
tight framing that withholds context
handheld or steadicam following, not leading
practical low-key light, source unclear

entries.why: The audience's first job is to work out what is happening, and that work buys their attention.
entries.how: No establishing shot, no name, no context. Coverage starts tight and only widens once the question is planted.

entries.name: The Two-Hander
entries.summary: Two people, one table, opposed objectives. All of it is in the cutting pattern.
entries.detail:
INT. DINER — LATE

MARA sits. The other side of the booth is empty. She has ordered for two.

DANIEL arrives eleven minutes late and does not apologise.

                    DANIEL
          You ordered.

                    MARA
          I ordered what you always get.
          That's not the same as ordering
          for you.

— The grammar: begin on a sustained two-shot so the geography is clear, move to matched over-the-shoulders as the objectives diverge, and cut to clean singles only at the moment one of them wins. Going to singles too early spends the escalation before it is earned.

prompt: sustained two-shot establishing geography before any coverage
matched over-the-shoulder singles on a normal to long lens
practical motivated light from a window or overhead fixture
static camera, cutting pattern carries the escalation

entries.name: Walk and Talk
entries.summary: Exposition delivered at speed while the world scrolls past behind it.
entries.detail:
INT. MINISTRY CORRIDOR — CONTINUOUS

They move. Everyone else moves around them.

                    ADEYEMI
          The committee sat at nine.

                    HOLLOWAY
          The committee sat at nine
          yesterday. Today it sat at seven,
          which is why you weren't in it.

A junior intercepts, hands over a folder, peels away without breaking anyone's stride.

— The device makes dense exposition watchable by giving the eye something to do. Needs a genuinely long unbroken take, a background populated with purposeful activity, and hand-offs that let new characters enter and leave without a cut.

prompt: long unbroken steadicam take tracking backwards ahead of the subjects
deep populated background with purposeful crossing activity
even practical institutional lighting, fluorescent
characters entering and exiting frame without a cut

entries.name: The Suspense Setup
entries.summary: Show the audience the bomb. Then refuse to mention it.
entries.detail:
INT. LECTURE HALL — DAY

We see, under the third row of seats, a canvas bag. Nobody in the room does.

The lecture begins. It is about eighteenth-century drainage.

A student in the fourth row drops a pen. It rolls forward. Under the third row.

She reaches for it.

— The distinction is surprise versus suspense: a bomb that explodes without warning buys ten seconds, a bomb the audience knows about buys the whole scene. Coverage must include the object regularly enough that the audience cannot forget it, and never so pointedly that the characters seem stupid.

prompt: recurring insert of the threat object, low and unmotivated by any character POV
otherwise ordinary neutral coverage of a mundane scene
slow push in as the scene proceeds
even naturalistic daylight, nothing ominous in the lighting

entries.name: Montage Sequence
entries.summary: Compress time by rhyming images. The cut does the arguing.
entries.detail:
MONTAGE — THE SEASON

—  Hands taping a wrist. Fresh tape.
—  The same hands. The tape is grey.
—  A locker door. Three photographs.
—  The same door. One photograph.
—  Hands taping a wrist. The wrist is thinner.

END MONTAGE

— The unit of meaning is the pair, not the shot: A next to B says something neither says alone. Matched framing across the cuts is what makes the comparison legible, so shoot the rhyming pairs on the same lens from the same position.

prompt: matched framing and identical lens across rhyming shots
same camera position between paired images
consistent lighting so the change reads as time, not setup
tight insert scale, detail rather than context

entries.name: The Reveal
entries.summary: Reframe everything already seen without contradicting any of it.
entries.detail:
INT. RECORDS OFFICE — NIGHT

He finds the file. Reads it standing up.

The signature at the bottom of the intake form is his own.

He does not react. He reads it again.

— The requirement is that the reveal be re-readable: every earlier scene must still make sense, and ideally make *more* sense. The shot is usually held long and static, because the audience needs time to do the arithmetic and a cut would take it away from them.

prompt: long static hold on the moment of realisation, no cut
insert of the revealing detail, held longer than comfortable
no music-cue framing, no push in
flat unhelpful light — the image withholds any interpretation

entries.name: Chase Geography
entries.summary: Speed is felt only if the space is understood. Establish, then accelerate.
entries.detail:
EXT. MARKET — DAY

Wide: the market runs east to west. A gate at each end.

RHYS enters from the east gate. Two men enter behind him.

He goes west. He has three hundred metres and no plan.

— The rule everyone breaks: a chase cut fast without an establishing geography is noise. Open wide, name the two endpoints, and only then cut to speed — every subsequent shot is legible because the audience knows which way is west.

prompt: opening extreme wide establishing both endpoints of the route
consistent screen direction maintained through every cut
camera at subject height, moving with rather than watching
hard directional sunlight, strong shadow for depth cues

entries.name: Kitchen-Sink Realism
entries.summary: Ordinary people in real rooms, and the drama is economic.
entries.detail:
INT. FLAT, KITCHEN — MORNING

The boiler is making the noise again. NADIA hits it. It stops.

                    NADIA
          Don't tell your dad.

                    SAM
          He'd have to be here.

She puts two slices in the toaster. Presses it down. It comes back up.

— The register: no scene begins with a line that announces its subject. Conflict arrives through objects and money. Shoot in the real room at its real size, on available light, with the camera in the position an actual person would stand.

prompt: real location at true scale, cramped framing forced by the room
available window light only, mixed with practicals
camera placed where a person would stand, eye level
desaturated northern palette, no colour styling

entries.name: The Bottle Episode
entries.summary: One location, no exits, and the constraint generates the drama.
entries.detail:
INT. SERVER ROOM — NIGHT

The door has locked. It locked forty minutes ago. They have discussed this.

                    OKONKWO
          Say it again.

                    PRIYA
          I'm not saying it again.

                    OKONKWO
          Say it again, because the first
          time you said it there were four
          of us in here.

— Written for constraint and then discovered to be the best tool available: with nowhere to cut away to, every escalation has to come from character. Coverage must find new geometry in one room, so blocking changes rather than locations.

prompt: single interior location, exits visible and closed
blocking that finds new angles within one room
hard practical sources — server LEDs, emergency lighting
progressively tighter framing as the scene escalates

entries.name: Opening / Closing Rhyme
entries.summary: End on the first image, changed. The difference is the film.
entries.detail:
OPENING — EXT. JETTY — DAWN
A man stands at the end of a jetty, facing the water. He does not go in.

CLOSING — EXT. JETTY — DAWN
A man stands at the end of a jetty, facing the water. Behind him, a second set of footprints in the frost.

— The pair must be shot identically — same lens, same position, same time of day — so the single altered element carries all the meaning. Shooting them on different days at different focal lengths is the most common way this device quietly fails.

prompt: identical framing, lens and camera position to the paired shot
same time of day and light direction
one deliberate compositional element changed
static locked-off camera, long hold

entries.name: Unreliable POV
entries.summary: Shoot subjective truth as though it were objective. Correct it later.
entries.detail:
INT. RESTAURANT — NIGHT (AS REMEMBERED)

The table is by the window. The light is warm. She is laughing.

INT. RESTAURANT — NIGHT (AS IT WAS)

The table is by the kitchen door. The light is green. She is not laughing.

— The rule is that the first version must be shot with complete conviction — no soft focus, no hint that it is a memory — because the moment the camera signals unreliability the device is spent. The two passes differ in light and blocking, never in grammar.

prompt: identical shot grammar in both passes, no dream signalling
difference carried entirely by light colour and blocking
no soft focus, vignette or memory convention
same lens and coverage pattern in both versions

entries.name: The Procedural Beat
entries.summary: Competence shown, not stated. Watch the work happen at its real speed.
entries.detail:
INT. WORKSHOP — DAY

She measures. Marks. Measures again. Cuts.

The cut is wrong by two millimetres. She does not swear. She takes a second piece of stock and starts again.

No dialogue. Four minutes.

— Process scenes work at real duration or not at all: compressing them into a montage converts expertise into a plot point. Inserts must be genuinely informative — a hand doing the actual thing, framed so the technique is readable.

prompt: informative macro inserts, technique readable in frame
real duration, minimal cutting
practical work lighting, task-lit hands
no music, no reaction cutaways

entries.name: Ensemble Introduction
entries.summary: Six people in four minutes, each defined by one action.
entries.detail:
INT. CREW ROOM — MORNING

BARRETT is already there. He is always already there.

SHIRIN arrives with three coffees and hands out two.

DAVIES arrives with nothing and takes one of the two.

MOSS arrives, sees this, says nothing, and writes it down.

— Each introduction is a single behaviour that will still be true in the last act. The coverage must let each action land cleanly, which usually means a wide that holds the room and singles only for the beat that defines each person.

prompt: sustained wide holding the whole ensemble and the room
one clean single per character, only on their defining action
even practical overhead lighting, no favouritism
staging that establishes relative status by position

entries.name: The Silent Climax
entries.summary: Strip the sound at the loudest moment. The audience leans in.
entries.detail:
EXT. STADIUM — NIGHT

Eighty thousand people are making a noise that can be felt in the chest.

He steps up.

SILENCE.

Not slow motion. Just the sound gone. His breathing. The ball. Nothing else.

— Works because it is a subjective device masquerading as a technical one: removing the crowd puts the audience inside the character's attention. Do not pair it with slow motion — using two devices at once means neither is trusted.

prompt: real-time motion, no slow motion
tight subjective framing, shallow focus isolating the subject
background crowd defocused into abstract light
hard stadium top light, strong rim separation

entries.name: The Arrival
entries.summary: A stranger enters a closed world. Shoot the world's reaction, not the stranger.
entries.detail:
EXT. VILLAGE ROAD — MIDDAY

A figure on the road, a long way off.

A child sees. The child does not run to tell anyone; the child goes inside.

A shutter closes. Then another.

By the time the figure reaches the well, the street is empty and every window is occupied.

— The mistake is covering the arrival from the stranger's side. The scene belongs to the place: shoot the doors closing, the watching, the emptiness, and let the stranger stay at a distance until the community has finished describing itself.

prompt: extreme wide with the approaching figure small and distant
coverage weighted to the reacting community, not the arrival
hard midday sun, deep-set shadow in doorways and windows
static camera, long lens compression down the road

entries.name: The Interrogation
entries.summary: One room, two chairs, and a table that decides who has power.
entries.detail:
INT. INTERVIEW ROOM 2 — TIME UNCLEAR

CONWAY sits. VOSS sits opposite. Between them, a folder Voss has not opened.

                    VOSS
          I'm going to open this.

                    CONWAY
          Then open it.

                    VOSS
          I'm going to open it in a minute.

He does not open it.

— Power is expressed geometrically. Whoever is shot from the lower angle is losing. The classical progression tightens the singles by a shot size each time the pressure rises, so the last exchange is in a scale the scene has not used before.

prompt: matched singles with deliberately mismatched camera height
framing tightens by one shot size at each escalation
hard overhead fluorescent, unflattering top light
featureless walls, no depth cues, no window
